turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: I just got back from my trip to Kyoto. The temples were breathtaking, especially Kinkaku-ji.

turns.speaker: Bob
turns.text: That sounds amazing! How long were you there?

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Ten days. I also visited Arashiyama and the bamboo grove there.

turns.speaker: Bob
turns.text: Did you try any local food?

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Yes! I had kaiseki at a restaurant near Gion. It had seven courses and cost around 15000 yen.

turns.speaker: Bob
turns.text: Wow, that's quite the experience. What was your favourite temple?

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Definitely Fushimi Inari. The thousands of torii gates are unlike anything else.

turns.speaker: Bob
turns.text: How did you get around the city?

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Mostly by bicycle. I rented one near Kyoto station for 800 yen per day.

turns.speaker: Bob
turns.text: Smart. Did you stay in a traditional inn?

turns.speaker: Alice
turns.text: Yes, a ryokan in the Higashiyama district. The tatami rooms and onsen were incredible.

turns.speaker: Carol
turns.text: We need to ship the new auth service by the end of March. The main blocker is the OAuth2 token refresh logic.

turns.speaker: Dan
turns.text: I can take that. I'll also need to update the rate limiter to handle the new token expiry window.

turns.speaker: Carol
turns.text: Good. The rate limit should be 200 requests per minute per user.

turns.speaker: Dan
turns.text: Understood. What database are we using for token storage?

turns.speaker: Carol
turns.text: PostgreSQL with a Redis cache in front. TTL on the cache is 5 minutes.

turns.speaker: Dan
turns.text: And the secret rotation schedule?

turns.speaker: Carol
turns.text: Every 90 days. The ops team handles the rotation via the vault integration.

turns.speaker: Dan
turns.text: Does the new service need to support PKCE?

turns.speaker: Carol
turns.text: Yes, mandatory for mobile clients. Web clients can use the implicit grant but we're deprecating that.

turns.speaker: Dan
turns.text: Got it. I'll have a draft PR up by Friday.

turns.speaker: Carol
turns.text: Great. Make sure to add integration tests against the staging environment, not mocks.

turns.speaker: Eve
turns.text: I made sourdough bread for the first time last weekend. It took three days total.

turns.speaker: Frank
turns.text: Nice! What hydration did you use?

turns.speaker: Eve
turns.text: 75 percent. The starter was at 100 percent hydration and I fed it twice before baking.

turns.speaker: Frank
turns.text: How long did you bulk ferment?

turns.speaker: Eve
turns.text: About 5 hours at room temperature, around 23 degrees Celsius.

turns.speaker: Frank
turns.text: Did you do a cold retard?

turns.speaker: Eve
turns.text: Yes, overnight in the fridge, roughly 14 hours.

turns.speaker: Frank
turns.text: What temperature did you bake it at?

turns.speaker: Eve
turns.text: 250 degrees Celsius for the first 20 minutes with steam, then 230 for another 25 minutes.

turns.speaker: Frank
turns.text: Steam from a Dutch oven or a pan of water?

turns.speaker: Eve
turns.text: Dutch oven. I preheated it for 45 minutes before loading the dough.
